analyst_view.overall: Early view: Chelsea under Xabi Alonso were beaten 1-0 at Sunderland and are fifth, while Palace are bottom after four straight league defeats and Pierre Sage is expected to be sacked, with Thomas Frank reported as the leading candidate. Palace also play Real Sociedad in the Europa League on 26 November. A new Palace manager by early December could make them harder to break down, but Chelsea at home are still the clear favourites.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little lower: Chelsea looked blunt at Sunderland and are without Joao Pedro (quad), and a new Palace manager usually starts by tightening the defence. Palace have conceded 24 in 10, so Chelsea should score, but a 2-1 or 2-0 type game fits better than a high-scoring one.

corners.text: The site has 10.8 corners, 6.8 for Chelsea. I lean higher: Palace have conceded six non-penalty set-piece goals, the second-most in the league, so Chelsea will push for corners, and a bottom side defending deep at Stamford Bridge tends to concede a lot of them.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards, most of them for Palace. I agree: a struggling side chasing the ball usually picks up bookings, and Adam Wharton was sent off in the Europa League this month. Nothing in the news points clearly higher or lower.

shots.text: The site has 25.7 shots. I lean slightly higher because Chelsea should have a lot of the ball against the bottom side, and Sage himself says Palace create chances but do not finish them, so they will get some shots too. Mid to high 20s looks likely.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. I lean lower: Chelsea lost 63% of first-half duels and produced little at Sunderland, Alonso admitted they 'didn't produce enough', and Joao Pedro is out. Plenty of shots, but fewer on target than the figure.
